sample_unit: LLM extraction runs (>2,000 total, across 4 synthetic clinical genetics notes)

links.outcome: HPO extraction F1, precision, and mapping error rate with vs without real-time ontology retrieval grounding
links.effect: Mean F1 rose from 0.46 (SD 0.22) to 0.72 (SD 0.15) (p<0.001); mapping error rate fell from 40.9% to 7.8%; precision rose from 56% to 90%; inferred-phenotype hallucination rate not significantly increased (p=0.08).
links.quote: Tool augmentation significantly improved performance across all models.

links.outcome: Tool-augmented LLM HPO extraction performance compared with a commercial EHR-based HPO extraction tool
links.effect: Tool-augmented LLMs achieved higher F1-scores than the commercial benchmark and substantially greater recall for inferred phenotypes.
links.quote: Compared with the commercial benchmark, tool-augmented LLMs achieved higher F1-scores and substantially greater recall for inferred phenotypes.

unlisted_practices: Delivering real-time ontology grounding to LLMs via Model Context Protocol as a vendor-agnostic tool-calling mechanism

screen.practice: retrieval grounding via external tools / Model Context Protocol
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of adding real-time ontology retrieval grounding (via Model Context Protocol / tool-calling) to various LLMs compared to a baseline condition without tools for clinical phenotype extraction.
